title: What the CMIP7 update means for our Global Climate Scenarios
gist: Oxford Economics says the CMIP7 climate scenarios narrow the 2100 warming range to 1.6-3.3°C and drop a no-overshoot 1.5°C path; it keeps its scenario suite unchanged for now and treats high-emission paths as low-probability tail-risk stress tests.

insights.claim: CMIP7 narrows central 2100 warming estimates to 1.6-3.3°C from 1.5-4.7°C in CMIP6, the first reduction of the upper bound in four model generations.
insights.speaker: Duncan Campbell
insights.so_what: Lower plausible worst case reduces physical-risk tails in climate stress tests.

insights.claim: Scientists no longer see even a deliberate rollback of climate policy producing the coal-intensive 4.5-5°C world of RCP8.5, due to falling renewables costs, plateauing global coal demand and over $2tn of annual clean-energy investment.
insights.speaker: Duncan Campbell
insights.so_what: Clean-energy economics have structurally changed the climate tail.
insights.locator: For the first time in four model generations

insights.claim: The lowest-emission CMIP7 scenario is warmer than before because the rapid 2020s emissions cuts assumed in CMIP6 did not materialise, so the world cannot realistically avoid overshooting 1.5°C even in the best case.
insights.speaker: Duncan Campbell
insights.so_what: 1.5°C-aligned targets rely on overshoot plus carbon removal; assume overshoot in planning.

insights.claim: Low-emission CMIP7 pathways rely heavily on large-scale carbon removal, which remains nascent.
insights.speaker: Duncan Campbell

insights.claim: The new CMIP7 'medium' scenario embeds currently implemented climate policies instead of a no-policy baseline, and scenarios are now named by emissions trajectory from 'high' to 'low-to-negative'.
insights.speaker: Duncan Campbell
insights.so_what: Better benchmark to assess policy weakening or strengthening.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics will keep its five long-term and two short-term climate scenarios largely unchanged, review them after the next NGFS long-term update due before year-end, and finish a baseline policy review in H1 2027.
insights.speaker: Duncan Campbell
insights.so_what: Scenario outputs used for stress tests and disclosure should stay stable near term.
insights.locator: How do Oxford Economics' climate scenarios compare?

insights.claim: Oxford Economics keeps its high-emission scenarios ('Climate Catastrophe', 'Climate Distress') as tail-risk stress tests and holds that carbon management plays an important but limited role that cannot substitute deep emissions cuts.
insights.speaker: Duncan Campbell
insights.so_what: Financial institutions should test above and below the current-policies baseline.
insights.locator: At the other end of the spectrum

insights.claim: An NGFS alignment to CMIP7 could materially affect financial institutions' stress-testing and corporates' strategic planning and reporting.
insights.speaker: Duncan Campbell
insights.so_what: Watch the NGFS update as the trigger for changed regulatory scenarios.
